decision: Report fleet LP lower bounds NOW for certified cells with an explicit bracket, instead of waiting for the lexicographic master. Demote the lexicographic work order below the initial-pool experiment.
rationale: Measured bus fixed cost is exactly 100000 while charging cost at the LP optimum is 86-2469 USD. For the combined-cost optimum x0 with route weight w and any minimum-fleet solution x*, 100000*w + C(x0) <= 100000*W* + C(x*) gives w - W* <= C(x*)/100000 <= ~0.025 at observed charging magnitudes. So the certified route weight brackets the true fleet LP bound to within about 0.03 buses. The lexicographic phase becomes a confirmation, not a blocker.
alternatives_rejected: (a) block all fleet claims until lexicographic CG exists -- rejected, the bracket is defensible and the data is in hand; (b) claim route_weight IS the fleet bound with no bracket -- rejected, that is the overclaim D0005 forbids

decision: Next algorithmic priority is the INITIAL POOL at k30/k40, ahead of the lexicographic master.
rationale: With --initial-pool singletons, k30 reaches route weight 77-107 against target 30 and k40 reaches ~302 against target 40 after 8h, with min_rc around -1.4e6 and -3.2e6: nowhere near converged. Historical k30/k40 runs that reached the target neighbourhood used matching- or GIRO-seeded pools. The binding constraint at large scale is therefore the initial pool, not the pricer.
alternatives_rejected: (a) longer wall budgets on singleton pools -- rejected, the gap is orders of magnitude; (b) finer grids -- rejected, irrelevant to this failure

decision: CLOSED: the exact pricer does match GIRO's fleet at small scale. All three k2 cells reach route weight exactly 2.0000 certified at 1 kWh / 5 min; 7 of 9 k2/k3/k5 cells reach their exact target. The binding discretization is TIME (block_min), not SOC.
rationale: Two controlled comparisons at fixed 1.0 kWh SOC changing only block_min 10->5: k02_s2 2.1538->2.0000 and k02_s3 2.1400->2.0000. SOC refinement alone plateaus (k02_s2: 2.1875/2.1667/2.1538/2.1538 across 15/5/2.5/1.0 kWh), so refining SOC below ~2.5 kWh buys nothing. This refutes the 'GIRO uses 1% SOC division' explanation: 2.5 kWh already IS 1% of 300 kWh and does not close the gap.
alternatives_rejected: (a) attribute the gap to SOC granularity -- rejected, contradicted by the plateau; (b) rerun a full resolution ladder -- rejected, 30 sensitivity cells already answered it

decision: Every Ryan-Foster node uses certified two-phase column generation: Phase I minimizes artificial mass with zero-cost real routes; only a strictly positive conservative Phase-I dual bound certifies infeasibility; zero artificial mass enables an artificial-free fleet-only Phase II
rationale: This separates feasibility from economics. Phase I pricing uses reduced cost 0 minus trip duals. Phase II fixes artificials to zero and uses reduced cost 1 minus trip duals, yielding a certified fleet LP bound for the discretized route space. A positive primal artificial value alone never prunes.
alternatives_rejected: Finite Big-M feasibility inference

decision: Pause corrected branch-and-price after three nodes whose average constrained Phase-II pricing call exceeds 10x the root Phase-II pricing call, or when a bounded k2 run ends without proof
rationale: The adopted kill criteria make computational failure reportable rather than inviting unbounded local search. Pure pricing wall time and enumerated subproblem counts are fsynced in the node ledger, independent of master and checkpoint overhead.
alternatives_rejected: Continuing automatically with deeper or inexact pricing

decision: Close an open Ryan-Foster node when ceil(certified fleet lower bound - tolerance) reaches the integer fleet incumbent
rationale: Phase II minimizes fleet route count and every integer partition has integral fleet. A 2.187499971 lower bound plus a 3-bus incumbent proves that no 2-bus solution exists; requiring the fractional bound itself to reach 3 discards the integrality information and prevents a valid fleet proof.
alternatives_rejected: Using combined-cost bounds or claiming charging-cost optimality; the closure proves fleet only
